<solution>
No. Human USP50 (UniProt Q70EL3, ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase 50) has a canonical length of **339 amino acids**, while human RLN2 (UniProt P04090, prorelaxin H2) has a canonical length of **185 amino acids**. Twice RLN2 would be 370 aa, which exceeds USP50's 339 aa, so USP50 is only ~1.83× as long — not at least twice as long.
